title: MARCH 17th BALLOT
full_story:
Clay County voters will head to the polls Tuesday for the state’s Primary Election, with major statewide and local offices on the ballot.  Several competitive races will determine who advances to November, while others will effectively decide the next officeholder because no opponent is running in the General Election.

Republican ballots will feature 6 Choices for Dick Durbin’s senate seat, and 4 candidates including Clay County farmer Darren Bailey for governor.  For the County Board there is a race for District 8, voters, they will choose between John Bayler, Jonathan Piperakis and Rod Franklin.  For Judge of the circuit there are 4 choices, Clay County States Attorney Phillip Givens, Aaron Jones, Wesley Gozia and Brenda Mathis.

Democratic Ballots will feature 10 people running for Dick Durbin’s senate seat and 4 choices for Comptroller.

All voters will decide if the sale of retail alcoholic liquor be prohibited in Larkinsburg Township, there is also a Clay County special tax for highway purposes question, and a question to opt into the federal program that would provide public K – 12 private school, and homeschool students with privately donated funds.

title: 2 VEHICLE WRECK ON US 50
full_story:
On Thursday at about 3 pm Marion County Sheriff’s Deputies say a car driven by 20-year-old Bradley Cantrell of Iuka was traveling west on Route 50 when he made a left turn into the Iuka General Store in front of a car driven by 42-year-old Julie Pottorff of Flora.

Cantrell was taken to Salem Township Hospital for treatment.  Pottorff and a passenger, 33-year-old Brian Cantrell, escaped injury.

US 50 traffic was blocked during investigation and cleanup of the scene.

title: FLORA PRE K SCREENING
full_story:
Parents of all 3 year and 4-year-old children residing in Flora Community Unit School District are invited to bring their children to the district’s pre-k screening.  If your child is currently enrolled as a preschool student or has previously been screened you DO NOT need to have another screening.

The screenings will be held on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday at the First Christian Church, located on the corner of North Main and West 4th Street.

Parents should make an appointment by going to the Flora School website to complete the Pre-K Screening Form, and you will be contacted with a screening time for your child.  If you have any questions, call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs.

Pre-K Students must have family income documentation on file in order to determine eligibility for the program.  Parents should bring income information, certified birth certificate, immunization record, lead screening result, Social Security Number, and school physical for their child to be in the Pre-K Program.

The Flora Unit # 35 P.A.T Prevention Initiative will be offering free developmental screenings for children ages birth to three during the Flora Pre-K Screenings.  Early detection of developmental delays will benefit a child for a lifetime.  If you are interested, please call 618-662-2014 and ask for Bristol Burroughs to make an appointment.

title: BRIDGE REPLACEMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced the closure of Old US 50 between Cedar Elm Drive and Country Road 800 E in Clay County, for a bridge replacement project over Raccoon Creek.  Work is expected to begin today, and be completed by August.

A detour will be posted directing traffic to use U.S. 50 between Xenia and Flora.  This project will improve safety and the smoothness of the pavement along Old US 50 for the traveling public.

Motorists will need to follow the posted detour or find an alternate route.  Drivers should allow extra time for trips through this area, pay close attention to changed conditions and obey the posted speed limits.

title: BREAKFAST BITES AND BUSINESS
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is sponsoring a Social Media Workshop titled Breakfast Bites and Business Insights on Wednesday, March 25th.

This session, presented in partnership with America’s SBDC Illinois and Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Business & Industry, will focus on how to effectively use social media to benefit and grow your business. Participants will enjoy light breakfast bites while gaining valuable insights from the featured speaker, Chris Forde, Program Director of Marketing and Communications for IECC.  Participants will learn practical tips, strategies, and tools to strengthen your online presence and better connect with your audience.

Whether you’re just getting started or looking to improve your current social media efforts, this workshop is designed to help your business shine online.  The workshop is free for Chamber Members and $5 for non members and will start at 8:30 am on Wednesday March 25th.  Space is limited RSVP today: https://forms.gle/Z46Cs5MCa1izi3ZYA

title: ENERGY ASSISTANCE AVAILABLE
full_story:
The Energy Assistance Foundation, through its Warm Neighbors Cool Friends (WNCF) program, partners with CEFS Economic Opportunity to provide energy bill payment assistance to eligible Ameren Illinois customers in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby counties.  In December 2025, Ameren Illinois contributed an additional $2 million to support Illinois households in 2026, ensuring more families can keep the lights on, stay warm in the winter, and cool in the summer.

Through this program, eligible households may receive up to $500 in assistance during the heating season, and up to $400 during the cooling season.

A matching customer payment made within the last 45 days is required.  The WNCF program serves income-qualified households who may not qualify for federal assistance but are still facing real financial strain.  Eligibility includes customers with household incomes between 200% and 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) or up to 80% of the county’s Area Median Income (AMI).

“This program is about peace of mind,” said Susan Sams, Executive Director of the Energy Assistance Foundation.  “Warm Neighbors Cool Friends is a critical lifeline for hardworking families who are doing their best but still need help covering essential energy costs.”

Funding is limited and applications are required.  Residents are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure they don’t miss out on available assistance.

For more information and to apply visit www.warmneighborscoolfriends.org/  OR http://www.cefseoc.org/liheap

title: BILL TO BENEFIT STUDENTS
full_story:
Illinois lawmakers are considering a bill that would opt Illinois into a new federal program providing donor money for students’ educational needs.

Senate Bill 3776, introduced by Senator Adriane Johnson, would opt Illinois into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program.  The program gives privately donated money to eligible K-12 students while providing a tax credit to the donors.

If the state does not opt into the program, Illinois students cannot receive the money.  But donors will get the tax credit anyway.

A recent poll conducted for the Illinois Policy Institute showed that almost 55% of Illinoisans support opting into the program, and only about 22% oppose or strongly oppose doing so.  Opting in gained more support than opposition across ages, regions, race and political ideology.

Starting in 2027, the scholarship money can be used by students in public, private or homeschools for educational services such as tutoring, additional classes, books or online educational materials, fees for standardized or college admissions exams and fees for dual enrollment.

That means public school students who may be struggling in certain academic areas or need extra help or materials won’t have to leave their local public school for the support or opportunities they need.

The program is good news for struggling Illinois students.  Recent test scores show just over half of the state’s third- through eighth-graders were reading at grade level last spring, and just 39% were proficient in math.  The scholarship program offers families a way to provide the additional academic support children need.

The program will not divert federal or state money from public schools to fund the scholarships.  There is no cost to states, only the benefit of more help for students.

The only cost to the federal government is minimal forgone income tax revenue.  The scholarships are donated by taxpayers, who will get an annual dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 for a qualified contribution to a scholarship-granting organization.

If Illinois fails to opt into the federal scholarship program, its residents can still obtain the tax credit by donating to a scholarship granting organization.  But that money would go to another state, no Illinois students would be eligible.

It’s not a good look for teachers unions or other opponents of the federal scholarships, who falsely say the program takes money from public education.  The program promises to add money from donors to address public, private and homeschool students’ needs.

The Federal Scholarship Tax Credit Program is a win-win-win for families and students and for Illinoisans who donate.  It provides money for students’ educational needs, it provides a tax credit to donors, and it takes no money from public schools.
